questions.question: A cereal box is a rectangular prism. Its net is cut out and laid flat, and it is made of exactly 6 rectangles: two are 20 cm by 30 cm, two are 20 cm by 10 cm, and two are 30 cm by 10 cm. What does the surface area of the box equal?
options: The sum of the areas of all 6 rectangles in the net
The sum of the areas of the 3 rectangles you can see
20 × 30 × 10, the amount of space inside the box
The total length of all the edges around the net
questions.explain: Surface area is every face added together, and a net lays all 6 faces out flat so you can total their areas. The usual trap is multiplying the three dimensions — that gives the space inside, not the covering outside.

questions.question: A net for a rectangular prism 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high is laid out flat. Its 6 rectangles have areas 24 cm², 24 cm², 18 cm², 18 cm², 12 cm² and 12 cm². What is the surface area of the prism?
options: 54 cm², one rectangle of each of the 3 sizes
108 cm², all 6 rectangle areas added up
72 cm³, found from 6 × 4 × 3 multiplied out
144 cm², six copies of the largest rectangle
questions.explain: Add every piece of the net: 24 + 24 + 18 + 18 + 12 + 12 = 108 cm². The answer of 72 comes from 6 × 4 × 3, which is volume — the space inside, not the total of the faces.

questions.question: A net for a cube is laid out flat. It is made of 6 identical squares, and each square has an area of 9 cm² because every edge of the cube is 3 cm. What is the cube's surface area?
options: 27 cm², just the three squares you can see
27 cm³, since 3 × 3 × 3 fills the cube
54 cm², every one of the 6 squares added
9 cm², the area of a single square face
questions.explain: A cube's net has 6 equal squares, so the surface area is 6 × 9 = 54 cm². Beware of 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, which fills the inside, and of adding only the faces you can see from one side.

questions.question: A net for a rectangular prism is cut out and laid flat. When it folds up, every rectangle in the net becomes one face of the prism. How many rectangle areas do you add together to find the surface area?
options: 3, because you only ever see 3 faces at once
8, because a rectangular prism has 8 vertices
12, because a rectangular prism has 12 edges
6, because the net folds into 6 flat faces
questions.explain: Surface area means all of the faces, and a rectangular prism folds up from 6 rectangles — the 3 hidden at the back count just as much. Answering 3 counts only what is visible and misses half the box.

questions.question: A right prism has two identical end faces, each with area B, and three rectangular side faces with areas P, Q and R. Which expression gives its surface area?
options: 2B + P + Q + R, with every face counted
B + P + Q + R, using just one end face
B × h, where h is the height of the prism
2B + 2P + 2Q + 2R, doubling every face
questions.explain: The net of a right prism holds both end faces plus each side rectangle exactly once, so the total is 2B + P + Q + R. B × h is the volume rule, and using a single B forgets the end face you cannot see.

questions.question: Noah peels the label off a soup can and it unrolls into a rectangle with an area of 220 cm². Each circular end of the can has an area of 28 cm². What is the total surface area of the can?
options: 56 cm², only the two circular ends added
276 cm², the label plus both circles
6160 cm², the rectangle times a circle
248 cm², the rectangle plus one circle
questions.explain: A cylinder's net is one rectangle and two circles, so the surface area is 220 + 28 + 28 = 276 cm². Leaving out the bottom circle is the usual slip — every piece of the net gets added, never multiplied.

questions.question: Maya is wrapping a rectangular gift box in paper with no overlap and no gaps. Which measurement does she need, and how does the box's net help her find it?
options: Volume: multiply the length, width and height
Surface area: add only the 3 rectangles she sees
Surface area: add the areas of all 6 rectangles
Perimeter: add the edges around the whole net
questions.explain: Wrapping covers the outside, so she needs surface area — the total of all 6 rectangle areas laid out in the net. Multiplying length by width by height answers a different question: how much fits inside.

questions.question: Ella's dollhouse roof is a right triangular prism 10 cm long. Each triangular end has an area of 6 cm², and its three rectangular faces measure 30 cm², 40 cm² and 50 cm². How much felt covers the whole outside of the roof?
options: 126 cm², one triangle plus the 3 rectangles
120 cm², only the 3 rectangular faces added
60 cm³, the triangle's area times 10 cm
132 cm², both triangles and 3 rectangles
questions.explain: The net of a triangular prism has 5 pieces — 2 triangles and 3 rectangles — so 6 + 6 + 30 + 40 + 50 = 132 cm². Counting the far triangle zero or one time, or working out 6 × 10, are the two classic errors; 6 × 10 is volume.

questions.question: Liam wants to paint the outside of a storage bin shaped like a rectangular prism, 50 cm by 40 cm by 30 cm. He writes 50 × 40 × 30 = 60 000 and says he needs enough paint for 60 000 cm². What went wrong?
options: He found the space inside, not the total face area
He multiplied the sides instead of adding them up
He counted only the three faces seen from the front
He left out the bottom face when he multiplied
questions.explain: Paint covers faces, so Liam needed the 6 rectangle areas from the net: 2(50×40) + 2(50×30) + 2(40×30) = 9400 cm². Multiplying all three dimensions gives volume, the space inside, which is measured in cm³.

questions.question: A community centre covers a rectangular pillar with vinyl. The pillar is 2 m by 1 m across and 3 m tall, and only the four side faces are covered — not the top or the bottom. Vinyl costs $12 per square metre. What is the total cost?
options: $264, from all six faces totalling 22 m²
$216, the four side faces total 18 m²
$108, only the two faces you can see
$72, using 2 × 1 × 3 = 6 for the pillar
questions.explain: Take only the four side rectangles from the net: 2(2×3) + 2(1×3) = 18 m², then 18 × $12 = $216. Working out 2 × 1 × 3 finds the space inside the pillar, which no amount of vinyl ever covers.

questions.question: Jasper builds a skateboard ramp shaped like a right triangular prism. Each end is a right triangle with legs 30 cm and 40 cm and a hypotenuse of 50 cm, and the ramp is 100 cm wide. He paints every outside surface, including the bottom. How much area does he paint?
options: 12 000 cm², the three rectangles added up
12 600 cm², one triangle end and 3 rectangles
13 200 cm², both ends plus all 3 rectangles
60 000 cm³, one triangle times the 100 cm width
questions.explain: Picture the net: 2 triangles at ½ × 30 × 40 = 600 cm² each, plus rectangles 30 × 100, 40 × 100 and 50 × 100, giving 1200 + 12 000 = 13 200 cm². Working out 600 × 100 gives volume, not the painted surface.

questions.question: Riya has two gift boxes that hold exactly the same amount. Box A is a cube 4 cm on every edge. Box B is a rectangular prism 8 cm by 4 cm by 2 cm. Which box needs more cardboard to build, once you compare the faces in each net?
options: Box A, because a cube's faces are biggest
Box A, because you see three 4 by 4 faces
Neither, both hold 64 cm³ so they match
Box B, since its six faces total 112 cm²
questions.explain: Equal volume does not mean equal surface area: box A's net totals 6 × 16 = 96 cm², while box B's totals 2(32 + 16 + 8) = 112 cm², so box B needs more cardboard. The space inside tells you nothing about the covering outside.
